title: Topic 6.2: Obligations of Children to Parents

pages.lesson:
LESSON: OBLIGATIONS OF CHILDREN TO PARENTS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.2: Obligations of Children to Parents
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Obligations of Children to Parents, part of Muamalaat (Social Relations) in Grade 4 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How do you show obedience and respect to your parents? 2. Why should children be dutiful towards their parent?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline obligations of children to their parents,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Children to Parents in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. assess the importance of obeying and respecting parents as a religious obligation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Children to Parents in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. demonstrate ways to obey and respect parents,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Children to Parents in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Obligations of Children to Parents in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. outline obligations of children to their parents,

   Obligations of Children to Parents helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. assess the importance of obeying and respecting parents as a religious obligation,

   Obligations of Children to Parents helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. demonstrate ways to obey and respect parents,

   Obligations of Children to Parents helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them.

   Obligations of Children to Parents helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the duties of children to their parents and present in class,

2. discuss the importance of obeying and respecting their parents (Q 17:23-24) and write the points in their notebook,

3. dramatise children’s obligations to their parents,

4. listen to qasidas/anashid (such as Ummy) on the importance of respecting and obeying parents from a digital device. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the duties of children to their parents and present in class,
2. discuss the importance of obeying and respecting their parents (Q 17:23-24) and write the points in their notebook,
3. dramatise children’s obligations to their parents,
4. listen to qasidas/anashid (such as Ummy) on the importance of respecting and obeying parents from a digital device. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Obligations of Children to Parents together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively is enhanced as learners describe the duties of children to their parents,

in groups, and present in class.

• Citizenship: the skill of social and cultural sensitivity and awareness is enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations

to their parents.

• Creativity and imagination: the skill of networking is enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations to their parents.

37

Values:
• Respect enhanced as learners respect each other’s opinion while discussing the importance of obeying and respecting their

parents.

• Responsibility enhanced as learners dramatise children’s obligations to their parents.

• Love enhanced as learners listen to qasidas/anashid (e.g. Ummy) on the importance of respecting and obeying parents from a

digital device.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Responsibility by relating well with parents and other members of the society.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Social Studies: as learners fulfil their duties and responsibility towards parents and other members of the society.

4. appreciate their parents by respecting and obeying them.

Remember the key question: How do you show obedience and respect to your parents? 2. Why should children be dutiful towards their parent?
